Daniel. An Israelite prophet and statesman who served foreign kings during the Babylonian exile, known for his unwavering faith and his ability to interpret visions and dreams.

Taken captive to Babylon as a young man during the exile of Judah, Daniel rose to prominence by interpreting dreams and visions for King Nebuchadnezzar and later for other Babylonian rulers. He refused to eat the royal food and wine, insisting instead on a vegetarian diet, yet he thrived and surpassed his peers in wisdom and beauty.

When he was punished for praying to God rather than obeying a decree to pray to the king, he was thrown into a lion's den. But God closed the lions' mouths and he emerged unharmed. His three companions, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, were cast into a fiery furnace for refusing to worship a golden image, yet they walked out of the fire unburned.

Daniel received visions of four great kingdoms that would rule the earth, using symbolic imagery of beasts and metals to depict future political powers. He spoke of the Son of Man, a messianic figure who would come in glory, language that later influenced New Testament descriptions of Jesus. His life and prophecies are recorded in the book of Daniel, the only substantial prophetic work in Hebrew scripture written primarily in Aramaic.
